summary:
I built the Descent 3 1.4 pilot patch exactly as the diagnosis concluded, and the check agrees with it. When the game enters flight (SM_GAME), it sizes the view from the pilot file's saved game_window_w/h and then clamps that to the display (Descent3 source: game.cpp SetScreenMode -> InitGameScreen). The staged pilot saved 640x480, so the view stays a 640x480 box even though -Width/-Height switch the display to 1920x1080. The patch writes 4096x4096 into the pilot. The clamp then turns that into the display mode on every box, which is why one staged constant is correct on both the LCDs and the CRTs.

What the script checks before patching:
- It searched the whole staged Descent3 tree for *.plt case-insensitively. Exactly one pilot exists, sdf.plt (1770 B, md5 b03f1b0f19e6d430f3d64b8c426f4da6). No other pilot is staged anywhere in the tree, and none in the _patches backup either.
- It walks the pilot header using the layout in pilot_class.cpp: version, name, ship, 5 custom strings, picture_id, difficulty, profanity, audiotaunts, hud_mode/stat/graphical_stat, then w and h. This is done by parsing because the offsets move with the length of the pilot name.
- It asserts version 0x2A, name 'sdf', that the parse lands on 0x1F/0x23, that the values are 640/480, and that bytes 0x1F..0x26 are exactly 80020000e0010000. Only then does it write 0010000000100000.
- After writing, it confirms that only those 8 bytes changed and that the file parses back as 4096x4096.

The built file differs from the original only at 0x1F..0x26. It differs from the test pilot already verified on .240 (rvw.plt.test-pilot) only in the 3 name bytes (rvw -> sdf). So what I built is byte-for-byte what was proven on hardware. The parser also reads the two pilots the game rewrote during testing (version 0x2B, from .195 and .240) correctly: 640x480 at 0x1F.

The launchers: 'Play Descent 3.bat' does NOT select a pilot, so every start stops at the PILOTS dialog; it needs `-pilot SDF` (details below). 'Join Descent 3 - LAN.bat' already passes `-pilot SDF`. 'Host Descent 3 - LAN.bat' runs the dedicated server, which has no pilot and no 3D view, so it is unaffected.

--check and --build ran. --publish is implemented and was NOT run. No share writes, no box touched.
launcher_changes_needed: scripts/fleet/stage-fleetres.py, TITLES['Descent3']['launchers']['Play Descent 3.bat']: change the replacement string from 'start "" "%~dp0main.exe" -launched -Width %FR_W% -Height %FR_H%' to 'start "" "%~dp0main.exe" -launched -pilot SDF -Width %FR_W% -Height %FR_H%'. Without -pilot SDF every start stops at the PILOTS dialog. That is worse than a lost click: a player who creates a NEW pilot there gets game_window = Video_res_list[Current_video_resolution_id], the Video-menu slot (640x480), not -Width (pilot_class.cpp pilot::initialize). The small box then comes back for that pilot. The current match regex re.escape('start "" "%~dp0main.exe" -launched') is a prefix of the new line too, so check that re-running the generator does not insert the switches twice (stage-fleetres.py --check must stay clean after two applies). Optional: add -nointro, which the Join launcher already uses.
'Join Descent 3 - LAN.bat' (hand-written in the library, no generator): NO change. It already passes -pilot SDF -Width %FR_W% -Height %FR_H%.
'Host Descent 3 - LAN.bat': NO change. It runs the dedicated server (-dedicated Dedicated.cfg), which has no pilot and no 3D window.

agent/shared/gameres.h and provisioning/fleetres/fleetres.c: NO change. The pilot is binary and InitGameScreen clamps 4096x4096 to each box's display, so one staged constant is right everywhere. There is nothing per-box for GAMERES to write, and adding a writer would create a second writer of sdf.plt that fights the game's own rewrite.

Library docs, following the staged-game loop, in the fix phase: Descent3/requires.json should drop "requires_capabilities": ["disc_mount"]. It is stale since the 1.4 no-CD main.exe and it is title-level, so under gamegate rules 6/7 it suppresses the shortcuts on a box with no mounter (.123). Also drop the 'relative mouse deltas / not automatable' note, which was refuted on .195/.240. Descent3/README-FLEET.txt needs the same correction plus the pilot-window cause. provisioning/fleetres/PER-TITLE-STATUS.md row 84 ('Descent3 | 1080p | main.exe -Width/-Height') must say 1080p needs BOTH the switches AND the staged sdf.plt with game window 4096x4096. Optional and cosmetic: RS_bitdepth=32 in install.reg.

Optional, not recommended as the default: -aspect 1.78 on 16:9 panels (from FR_ASPECT). Measured: it fixes the 1.33x stretch but shrinks the vertical FOV and pushes the cockpit monitors off the bottom of the screen. It is a taste call and separate from this patch.
tests: python3 -m pytest -q tests/python/test_patch_descent3.py -> 15 passed in 0.32s (the share was mounted, so the two share tests ran rather than skipped). Pure-logic coverage on synthetic pilots: offsets 0x1F/0x23 for 'sdf', offsets shift with the name length, exactly 8 bytes change, both the old value (640) and the new value (4096) are asserted, refusal on version 0x2B / wrong old values / a parse that lands elsewhere / truncated or garbage input, the original/patched/unknown states, a case-insensitive *.plt finder, and build plus the publish ordering on a fake library with _put/_share_md5 stubbed (already patched -> no put; original -> backup then live, in order; an unknown share md5 -> refuse; a failed backup -> stop before touching the live file). Share tests: the staged tree holds exactly sdf.plt, and the staged file is the original and patches to md5 a42937534d704dce2374df0a0deea849 (or is already that). They skip loudly if /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games-Library is absent. apply.py --check -> OK (original, would patch 80020000e0010000 -> 0010000000100000). apply.py --build -> ~/.retro-fleet/patch-out/descent3/Descent3/sdf.plt, 1770 B, md5 a42937534d704dce2374df0a0deea849. Log: .claude/evidence-1080p/build-descent3/check-build.log.
risks: The game rewrites sdf.plt at the first mission start on each box: version 0x2A->0x2B, 1770->1772 B, and it saves the CLAMPED size (e.g. 1920x1080, or the CRT's mode), not 4096. If that box later gets a larger display, the view stays at the old size until GAMESYNC recopies the staged pilot or the player presses '='. This is benign on the current fleet.

GAMESYNC and the rewritten pilot: once a box has played, its 1772 B copy differs in size from the staged one, so ANY later GAMESYNC over that title (RESET+START or an autodeploy generation) overwrites it with the staged pilot. That wipes the player's mission progress and control binds in that pilot. The same thing happens today with the unpatched pilot. The window stays correct, because 4096 is re-clamped.

Getting the fix onto boxes: GAMESYNC never re-runs on a provisioned box by itself (it checks the gamesync.done marker). The published pilot therefore reaches a box only through GAMESYNC RESET+START or the new autodeploy generation. Boxes still holding the original have the SAME SIZE (1770 B), so the push relies on mtime; sharewrite.py enforces a fresh mtime, which covers it. Boxes where the game already rewrote the pilot (1772 B) are recopied because the size differs.

The patch is only proven on pilot version 0x2A and on this exact file. apply.py refuses anything else (a new version, other values, or a parse that does not land on 0x1F/0x23). A new pilot staged later would stay 640x480, and --check FAILS on any unknown *.plt so that case cannot pass silently.

Leaving -pilot SDF out of 'Play Descent 3.bat' keeps the PILOTS dialog. A pilot the player creates there defaults to the Video-menu resolution (640x480 slot), which silently brings the small box back for that pilot.

Proportions: at full screen the 4:3 projection is stretched 1.33x on 16:9 (rend_GetAspectRatio assumes 4:3). The fix makes 1080p usable; it does not make the image Hor+. -aspect 1.78 has measured side effects (see launcher_changes_needed).

The in-game Video > Resolution menu still lists only 7 hardcoded 4:3 modes, none of them 1920x1080. Picking one there resizes to that mode (force_res_change) and overrides -Width/-Height for the session. The 1080p path is the launcher, not the menu; the engine offers no menu path to it.
hw_verification_plan:
FUTURE, after --publish and after the stage-fleetres.py change that adds -pilot SDF has shipped.

1. On the test box (.240 XP first, then .195 Win7, .123 and .145), purge the pilot: `EXEC cmd /c del "C:\Games\Descent3\sdf.plt"`. Then run `GAMESYNC RESET` + `GAMESYNC START` (or the autodeploy generation). Confirm `failed_files == 0` and `titles_done == titles_total` == the library count. Then DOWNLOAD C:\Games\Descent3\sdf.plt and check md5 a42937534d704dce2374df0a0deea849 and bytes 0x1F..0x26 = 0010000000100000.
2. Launch through the agent: `EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\Descent3" "Play Descent 3.bat"`. This is keyboard-navigable (refuted as non-automatable on .195/.240). Send UIKEY ESCAPE to skip the intro. The PILOTS dialog must NOT appear once -pilot SDF is in; if it does, the launcher change did not ship.
3. Main menu: UP x3, RETURN (New Game), DOWN, RETURN (Pilot Training). Wait about 25 s.
4. DISPLAYCFG must read 1920x1080 (x16) on the LCD boxes. Take SCREENSHOT 0 in flight; GDI captures this title on XP and on Win7 .195. The screenshot must show the 3D view filling the whole 0..1919 x 0..1079 frame, with no black border. Today it is a box at x=640..1280, y=300..780. On a CRT box (.124/.143) the view must fill that box's own mode.
5. Must NOT change:
   - Host LAN (dedicated server: TCP/UDP 2092 LISTENING, 'Opening level').
   - Join LAN (main.exe -pilot SDF -directip +connect <ip> still reaches the host, with the join rendering full screen).
   - The dev-host Wine descent3-server.
   - The Video-menu list, which stays the 7 hardcoded 4:3 modes.
   Multiplayer is client-side unaffected: the pilot's window size is not sent on the wire.
6. Clean up: taskkill /f /im "main.exe"; delete C:\Games\Descent3\custom\cache\d3s*.tmp and .lock. Expect sdf.plt on the box to become 1772 B (version 0x2B) with 1920x1080 saved. That is the game's normal rewrite, not a failure; record it rather than restoring it.
7. Then push the title to every other connected box (purge sdf.plt + GAMESYNC) per the staged-game loop.
review_notes:
I found nothing in the diagnosis to overrule. It is confirmed three ways:
- the Descent3 source release: pilot::read/read_hud_data layout, and SetScreenMode(SM_GAME) -> InitGameScreen, which clamps to Max_window_w/h;
- the two 0x2B pilots rewritten on hardware, which parse to 640x480 at 0x1F;
- the hardware-verified rvw.plt, which is byte-identical to my output except for the name.

Additions to the diagnosis:
(a) The offsets depend on the pilot name's length, so the script parses the header rather than trusting fixed offsets. It still asserts 0x1F/0x23 as the task required.
(b) A new pilot's default window is the Video-menu slot resolution (pilot::initialize), which strengthens the case for -pilot SDF in 'Play Descent 3.bat'.
(c) requires.json's title-level disc_mount is not only stale: under gamegate rules 6/7 it suppresses every Descent 3 shortcut on a box with no mounter (.123).

The source files I fetched from github.com/DescentDevelopers/Descent3 (GPL) are kept only as evidence under build-descent3/src, not in the git tree. Nothing was committed, per the phase rules. Nothing under provisioning/patches/descent3 contains game data: apply.py holds only an 8-byte original-value assertion and md5s.
